reproduction_target: Chromatin-state and 3D-connectivity characterisation of poised enhancers (PEs) across the HNES1 naive-to-primed human pluripotent stem cell transition. Computational target: design of a Poised Enhancer Capture Hi-C (PECHi-C) system from published ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN (bowtie2 v2.3.5 -> MACS2 v2.1.1 -> ChIPQC v1.21.0 -> DpnII fragment mapping); metaplot generation from public ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN BAMs (deepTools v3.5.4 bamCoverage/bigwigAverage/computeMatrix/plotHeatmap); PECHi-C primary processing (HiCUP 'combinations' branch v0.7.4 -> chicagoTools v1.30.0 -> CHiCAGO v1.30.0 -> makePeakMatrix.R) with plotBaits/peakEnrichment4Features and plotgardener v1.6.4 visualisation; CUT&Tag primary processing (samtools v1.20, deepTools v3.5.6) and DpnII-bin pileups cross-normalised with DESeq2 v1.40.2 estimateSizeFactors; SparCC via SpiecEasi v0.1.5; PE annotation against the ENCODE cCRE 'enhancer decoration matrix' and the VISTA Enhancer Browser (data.table v1.17.6 foverlaps, ggplot2 v3.5.2); Dynamic-Time-Warping temporal clustering of PE contacts (dtwclust v5.5.12 tsclust, UpSetR v1.4.0); K-means clustering of chromatin/TF features (ppclust v1.1.0.1); chi-square contingency enrichment; GO enrichment (clusterProfiler v4.8.2, GOSemSim v2.26.1); network rewiring analysis (igraph v2.0.3, ggraph); PRC2-perturbation RNA-seq (Babraham platform pipeline -> featureCounts/Subread v2.0.8 with Gencode v47 -> DESeq2 v1.40.2, org.Hs.eg.db v3.17.0, AnnotationDbi v1.62.2); calibrated CUT&Tag (TrimGalore v0.6.5 -> Nextflow bowtie2 --very-sensitive -I 10 -X 700 to GRCh38/BDGP6 -> samtools v1.21 MapQ>20 -> spike-in scale factors -> deepTools v3.5.6 -> bwtool v20170428 -> DESeq2); PRC2-perturbation PECHi-C reprocessing and connectivity analysis (custom R script + DESeq2); integrative Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis statistics (rstatix v0.7.2); NE/DE differentiation chromatin-state analysis; and 4C-seq processing (fastp v0.23.4 -> pipe4C -> IGV, 4DN dataset 4DNFI2YA1USU). Cell culture, the naive-to-primed transition, CUT&Tag / calibrated CUT&Tag / ChIP-seq / RNA-seq / 4C-seq library generation, RT-qPCR, western blot and iCRISPRa perturbation are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v3 JATS source XML (WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403; a direct curl with a browser User-Agent returned HTTP 200 / 336,296 bytes and contained the complete 'MATERIALS & METHODS' -> 'Computational analyses' block and the 'RESOURCE AVAILABILITY' block). NOTE: a first curl into a shared /tmp filename was overwritten by a concurrently running sibling job and briefly yielded a different bioRxiv article (2025.12.09.693261, TNSEEK); the fetch was repeated into an isolated directory and the article identity was re-verified by grepping the title token 'Poising' before any scoring was done. No code repository exists yet: the availability statement says 'Data analysis scripts will be deposited on GitHub upon paper acceptance', so the Code axis is at most 1 (reconstructable from prose) for every step and is 0 wherever the step is a bespoke in-house analysis rather than a documented single-tool invocation. Newly generated sequencing data are likewise embargoed ('uploaded to GEO ... All the data will be made publicly available on paper acceptance') with no accession number quoted, so steps entering from this study's raw reads score data = 0; steps entering from the OSF-released processed matrices (https://osf.io/evcy6/) or from published GEO/ENCODE/VISTA/4DN resources score data = 2, and mixed-input steps score 1. Version scoring rule: a prose pin counts (version = 1) only when at least major.minor is given; pipe4C, IGV, the 'Nextflow implementation of bowtie2', the Babraham RNA-seq platform pipeline, ggraph and the ggplot2 calls in the cCRE/volcano sections carry no version. No lockfile, container, conda specification, renv.lock or release tag is claimed anywhere, so version is capped at 1 throughout.

steps.label: Wet-lab: hPSC culture (WA09/H9 primed, HNES1 naive, WTC11 iCRISPRa, Drosophila S2 spike-in cells) and the 14-day naive-to-primed transition sampled at days 0/1/3/5/7/10/14 in biological triplicate
Wet-lab: Poised Enhancer Capture Hi-C library generation with Agilent SureSelect custom biotinylated RNA probes against 32,142 DpnII fragments
Wet-lab: CUT&Tag for H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27me3, H3K27ac, H2AK119ub and IgG across the transition (150 bp paired-end)
Wet-lab: calibrated (Drosophila S2 spike-in) CUT&Tag for H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub under DMSO / PROTAC / UNC1999
Wet-lab: KAT3B/p300 ChIP-seq in naive and primed hPSCs (75 bp single-end)
Wet-lab: PRC2 perturbation (DMSO / PROTAC / UNC1999 at day 5) and rRNA-depleted RNA-seq library preparation, 3 biological replicates per condition
Wet-lab: RT-qPCR of DLX1, DLX2, METAP1D, GAPDH with 2^-ddCt quantification
Wet-lab: 4C-seq at the DLX1-DLX2 poised-enhancer viewpoint (DpnII / NlaIII, three biological replicates, 60 bp paired-end)
Wet-lab: western blot for H3K27me3, H4, EED, EZH2
Wet-lab: inducible CRISPR-activation (iCRISPRa) in WTC11 iPSCs targeting the DLX1-DLX2 poised enhancer

Alignment of six published ChIP-seq datasets plus CUT&RUN H3K4me1 (GSM4798822, GSM4798823) and H3K27me3 (released with this study) to GRCh38 with bowtie2 v2.3.5 - no bowtie2 flags, no index build recipe and no GRCh38 patch/analysis-set specified
Peak calling with MACS2 v2.1.1, --broad for H3K27me3, p-value cutoffs 1e-6.5 (ChIP-seq) and 1e-5 (CUT&RUN) derived from precision-recall against Rada-Iglesias 2011 H9 data
ChIP-seq quality metrics with the ChIPQC Bioconductor package v1.21.0; datasets with FRiP below 10% excluded

Capture design: intersection of ChIP-seq and CUT&RUN bivalent regions, exclusion of annotated gene promoters, and mapping of the resulting PE regions onto DpnII-digested genome fragments (32,142 baited fragments) - bespoke, no script, no promoter annotation source or version stated; the resulting GRCh38 fragment coordinates are released on OSF

BigWig generation from public ATAC-seq (GSM2698915-GSM2698922), input (GSM2698940-GSM2698942, GSM2901723-GSM2901725), H3K27me3 (GSM5569915/16/23/24), H3K4me1 (GSM4798820-GSM4798824) and this study's p300 ChIP-seq BAMs using deepTools v3.5.4 bamCoverage with default parameters, replicates combined with bigwigAverage

Metaplot generation: deepTools computeMatrix reference-point centred on each enhancer +/-10 kb with --missingDataAsZero, plotted with plotHeatmap using 'manually defined scales' for colourmap and heatmap; enhancer sets pre-filtered to 100-450 reads per 20 kb window

PECHi-C read processing, alignment and filtering with HiCUP v0.7.4, 'combinations' branch (https://github.com/StevenWingett/HiCUP/tree/combinations) - branch named but no commit hash; input raw reads are this study's own and are not yet deposited
CHiCAGO input file generation with chicagoTools v1.30.0, DpnII fragments binned to ~5 kb with baited PE-harbouring fragments left unbinned

Significant-interaction calling with CHiCAGO v1.30.0 'as previously described', other-end annotation with GENCODE v36 TSS, and cross-sample summarisation with makePeakMatrix.R (default parameters); full peak matrices released on OSF

Candidate-PE contact visualisation with Chicago::plotBaits() (baitIDs 1340 and 580854, max interaction distance 500 kb) and histone-modification enrichment of PE-interacting regions with peakEnrichment4Features()
Locus-specific combined PECHi-C + CUT&Tag figure panels with the plotgardener R package v1.6.4 - bespoke figure code, not released
CUT&Tag BAM sorting, indexing and merging of biological triplicates with samtools v1.20 - input BAMs derive from this study's undeposited reads
Conversion of merged and individual CUT&Tag BAMs to bigWig with deepTools v3.5.6 bamCoverage and track visualisation with plotgardener v1.6.4

CUT&Tag feature count matrices on the PECHi-C DpnII bins (baited fragments unbinned) cross-normalised with DESeq2 v1.40.2 estimateSizeFactors; RPKM at baited fragments computed by normalising counts to fragment length. Pileup matrices released on OSF but the binning/counting code is not

Sparse correlation of PECHi-C CHiCAGO scores across transition time points and H9 with SparCC as implemented in SpiecEasi v0.1.5 - no iteration count, exclusion threshold, bootstrap number or seed reported

PE annotation against the ENCODE 'enhancer decoration matrix' (https://downloads.wenglab.org/cCRE_decoration.matrix.1.gz) filtered to 635,906 cCREs active in at least one tissue, with cCRE coordinates from the UCSC encodeCcreCombined track, summarised to tissue level and plotted with ggplot2 (no version) - bespoke overlap/aggregation code not released, no UCSC download date

Overlap of PE baits with VISTA Enhancer Browser elements filtered to curation_status = 'positive' and human 'hs' identifiers, computed with data.table v1.17.6 foverlaps and plotted with ggplot2 v3.5.2 - no VISTA release date or download snapshot

Temporal clustering of 9,998 PE-TSS/PE-PE contacts (CHiCAGO score >5 in any dataset and >3 in at least one transition time point) by Dynamic Time Warping with dtwclust v5.5.12 tsclust, k tested 3-8, k = 6 chosen 'based on inspection of cluster trajectories' with clusters 2 and 6 merged post hoc; combinations visualised with UpSetR v1.4.0. No seed, no distance/centroid arguments, and a human-in-the-loop k selection

K-means clustering (k = 5) of arcsinh-transformed, DESeq2 estimateScalingFactorsForMatrix-normalised TF/co-factor/histone pileups at baited PE fragments, heatmaps via ppclust v1.1.0.1, plus H3K27me3 spreading counted as 10 bp bins with >25 reads within 20 kb of PE centres. Two input datasets (DPPA2/DPPA4 ChIP-seq) are cited as 'in revision' and are not publicly available; no k-means seed or nstart reported

Chi-square test on the 5x5 temporal-class x PE-cluster contingency table (chisq.test() in R) with a log-odds-ratio heatmap (formula given in prose) and |standardised residual| > 1.96 flagged, plotted with ggplot2 v3.5.2 - no script released

GO Biological Process enrichment per temporal class with clusterProfiler v4.8.2 (Benjamini-Hochberg correction), top 20 terms per condition in a dotplot, semantic grouping with GOSemSim v2.26.1 Wang method followed by hierarchical clustering into four semantic clusters - no OrgDb version, no gene universe definition, no GO release date, no hclust linkage or cut criterion

Network analysis of PE contact rewiring: adjacency matrix and Kamada-Kawai layout with igraph v2.0.3, then a 'zoomed in' subnetwork built from 50 randomly subsampled disjoint subgraphs supplemented with all HOX-gene contacts, drawn with ggraph (no version) using a Fruchterman-Reingold layout - both layouts and the subsampling are stochastic with no seed reported

PRC2-perturbation RNA-seq read QC and GRCh38 mapping 'performed by the Babraham Institute bioinformatics platform according to their pipeline' - no tool, no version, no parameters, no pipeline reference of any kind, and the reads themselves are not yet deposited

BAM sorting/indexing with samtools v1.20 and gene-level quantification with featureCounts (Subread v2.0.8) using default parameters and Gencode v47 annotation, counting only uniquely mapped exonic reads; per-sample matrices merged into a combined matrix

Differential expression with DESeq2 v1.40.2, design ~ condition + replicate, PROTAC vs DMSO and UNC1999 vs DMSO, BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 0.1; symbols annotated with org.Hs.eg.db v3.17.0 and AnnotationDbi v1.62.2; volcano plots with ggplot2 labelling padj < 1e-3 and |log2FC| > 0.41. Analysis table on OSF but neither the merged count matrix nor the script is released

Calibrated CUT&Tag primary processing: TrimGalore v0.6.5 trimming, then 'a Nextflow implementation of bowtie2' with --very-sensitive -I 10 -X 700 against GRCh38 (human) and BDGP6 (spike-in), MapQ > 20 filtering, sorting and indexing with samtools v1.21. The Nextflow workflow is unnamed, unversioned and unreleased; bowtie2 itself carries no version here

Spike-in scale-factor computation and generation of reference-calibrated bigWigs with deepTools v3.5.6 bamCoverage. The scale-factor formula is rendered as an inline image and is absent from the machine-readable text ('Scale factors were calculated as follows : .'), so the normalisation is not recoverable from prose

Conversion of calibrated H3K27me3 bigWigs to pileups over baited PE fragments with bwtool summary v20170428, then DESeq2 differential testing per perturbation vs DMSO (padj < 0.05 and negative log2FC = 'reduced'; padj > 0.5 = 'non-responsive'), and intersection of PROTAC- and UNC1999-depleted region sets. Pileup and analysis tables on OSF; no script

Density profiles and heatmaps for H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub across DMSO/PROTAC/UNC1999: replicate bigWigs merged with deepTools bigwigAverage, matrices from computeMatrix reference-point at PE centres +/-10 kb with --skipZeros, rendered with plotHeatmap and plotProfile

PRC2-perturbation PECHi-C reprocessing with HiCUP combinations + chicagoTools + CHiCAGO as in C7-C9, significant contacts called on replicate-pooled data per condition and visualised with plotGardener; for differential analysis two replicates each of PROTAC and UNC1999 were merged 'to balance sequencing depths' (which replicates is not stated)

Total connectivity per PE bait per replicate computed with 'a custom R script' (not released) and differential connectivity upon each PRC2 perturbation estimated with DESeq2 - the read-counts table is on OSF but neither the script nor the DESeq2 design/parameters are given

Integrative PECHi-C x CUT&Tag statistics: DESeq2 t-value distributions for perturbed vs intact PEs plotted with ggplot2 v3.5.1, Wilcoxon rank-sum and one-sample Wilcoxon tests, pairwise Wilcoxon with Bonferroni correction via rstatix v0.7.2, and a Kruskal-Wallis test on 1,590 single-class PE baits

NE/DE differentiation analysis: DESeq2 on CUT&Tag count matrices for H3K27me3, H3K4me1, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac (day 14 vs DE and day 14 vs NE, padj < 0.05), assignment of chromatin-state dynamics ('H3K27me3 down, H3K27ac up' = developmental activation), and log2 fold changes of arcsinh-CHiCAGO scores with pseudocount 0.1 per temporal contact class
4C-seq read trimming with fastp v0.23.4 requiring minimum length 45 bp, read 1 only retained for downstream analysis

4C-seq mapping and filtering with pipe4C (https://github.com/deLaatLab/pipe4C) at viewpoint chr2:172,096,280, minimum mapping quality 1, unique reads only, cis-only analysis, QC from the pipe4C diagnostic reports - no pipe4C version or commit, and no config/VPinfo file released

Visualisation of 4C interaction profiles (WIG export) in IGV (no version) alongside TAD boundaries in the DLX1-DLX2 region taken from public WTC11 Hi-C dataset 4DNFI2YA1USU from the 4DN data portal - no TAD-calling method, resolution or parameters stated

headline.static_readiness: 0/36 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 6/36 (17%) RI, 30/36 NI. The binding constraint is a double embargo. (1) Code: the availability statement says 'Data analysis scripts will be deposited on GitHub upon paper acceptance' - no repository exists today, so the Code axis is capped at 1 (reconstructable) and drops to 0 for the 20 steps that are bespoke in-house analyses (capture design, DpnII-bin counting, all clustering/annotation/network/statistics steps, the 'custom R script' for PE connectivity, and every figure panel). (2) Data: 'Sequencing data generated in this study have been uploaded to GEO ... All the data will be made publicly available on paper acceptance' - no accession number is quoted anywhere, so every step entering from this study's own raw reads (PECHi-C, CUT&Tag, calibrated CUT&Tag, p300 ChIP-seq, PRC2 RNA-seq, 4C-seq) scores data = 0. What partially offsets this is unusually good processed-data release: the OSF deposit https://osf.io/evcy6/ carries the DpnII fragment coordinates, the full CHiCAGO peak matrices, the CUT&Tag pileup matrices, the PRC2 expression analysis table and the connectivity read-count table, which lifts nine downstream steps to data = 2. The six RI steps (C1 bowtie2 v2.3.5, C2 MACS2 v2.1.1, C3 ChIPQC v1.21.0, C5/C6 deepTools v3.5.4, C10 CHiCAGO plotBaits/peakEnrichment4Features) are exactly the steps that combine a pinned single-tool invocation, stated parameters, and at least partly public input. Version is capped at 1 everywhere: prose pins are numerous and mostly exact (bowtie2 v2.3.5, MACS2 v2.1.1, ChIPQC v1.21.0, HiCUP v0.7.4, chicagoTools/CHiCAGO v1.30.0, samtools v1.20/v1.21, deepTools v3.5.4/v3.5.6, DESeq2 v1.40.2, plotgardener v1.6.4, SpiecEasi v0.1.5, data.table v1.17.6, dtwclust v5.5.12, UpSetR v1.4.0, ppclust v1.1.0.1, clusterProfiler v4.8.2, GOSemSim v2.26.1, igraph v2.0.3, ggplot2 v3.5.1/v3.5.2, Subread v2.0.8, org.Hs.eg.db v3.17.0, AnnotationDbi v1.62.2, TrimGalore v0.6.5, bwtool v20170428, rstatix v0.7.2, fastp v0.23.4) but there is no lockfile, container, conda spec, renv.lock or release tag, and no R/Bioconductor base version. Even under a successful stage-2 code check no step could exceed RI.
headline.coverage: 36 computational steps enumerated from the 'Computational analyses' block of the bioRxiv v3 Methods (capture design; metaplots; PECHi-C primary processing; CUT&Tag primary processing; sparse correlation; cCRE and VISTA annotation; temporal clustering; chromatin-feature clustering; enrichment testing; GO analysis; network analysis; PRC2 RNA-seq, CUT&Tag and PECHi-C; integrative statistics; NE/DE analysis; 4C-seq). 10 coarse wet-lab steps counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 36/46 (78%) of enumerated steps are C-layer.

gaps.missing: No code repository exists at the time of assessment. The verbatim statement in 'Data and code availability' is: 'Data analysis scripts will be deposited on GitHub upon paper acceptance.' No GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket URL for this study's own code, no Zenodo DOI, no Software Heritage identifier, no supplementary script archive. The only repository URLs in the paper point to third-party tools (https://github.com/StevenWingett/HiCUP/tree/combinations and https://github.com/deLaatLab/pipe4C). Twenty steps are explicitly bespoke (capture design C4, DpnII-bin count matrices C14, cCRE and VISTA annotation C16/C17, DTW and K-means clustering C18/C19, chi-square log-odds heatmap C20, GO pipeline C21, network construction C22, DESeq2 drivers C25/C28/C31/C33, calibrated-CUT&Tag scale factors C27, integrative statistics C32, all plotgardener/ggplot2 figure code) and cannot be reconstructed from prose at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis scripts now rather than at acceptance: the CHiCAGO/HiCUP driver configuration, the DpnII binning and pileup code, the dtwclust and K-means clustering drivers with their seeds, the DESeq2 model scripts for expression, H3K27me3 occupancy and PE connectivity, the custom connectivity R script, the annotation-overlap code, and all figure code, in a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo. None of this carries data-embargo risk.

gaps.where: Newly generated sequencing data (W2-W8 -> C7-C9, C12-C14, C19, C23-C30, C34-C36)
gaps.missing: No accession number is given for any dataset generated by this study. Verbatim: 'Sequencing data generated in this study have been uploaded to GEO. CUT&Tag data for the naive-to-primed transition are available at GEO. All the data will be made publicly available on paper acceptance.' There is no GSE identifier, no reviewer token, and no release date, so PECHi-C, CUT&Tag, calibrated CUT&Tag, p300 ChIP-seq, PRC2 RNA-seq and 4C-seq raw reads are unobtainable. In addition, the DPPA2/DPPA4 ChIP-seq used in C19 is cited as 'A. Malcolm, P.R.G et al., in revision' with no accession at all, and the H3K27me3 CUT&RUN used in C1 is 'released with this study'.
gaps.how_to_close: Quote the GSE accession (with a reviewer access token during embargo) in the availability statement, and give an accession or an interim deposit for the DPPA2/DPPA4 ChIP-seq cited as in revision. Where the embargo must hold, state the intended release date explicitly.

gaps.where: Intermediate datasets released on OSF (https://osf.io/evcy6/) and Tables S1-S4
gaps.missing: The OSF deposit is referenced six separate times (DpnII fragment coordinates, full CHiCAGO peak matrices, CUT&Tag pileup matrices, PRC2 expression analysis table, calibrated H3K27me3 analysis table, PECHi-C connectivity read-count table) but always as a bare project URL with no file names, no per-file checksums, no version/registration and no schema description. Table S1-S4 contents (temporal cluster assignments, PE feature clusters, PRC2 contact and occupancy results, NE/DE chromatin-state assignments) are the sole machine-readable link between many downstream steps and are distributed only as supplementary files.
gaps.how_to_close: Create an OSF registration (frozen, DOI-bearing) rather than a live project, list the exact file name and sha256 for each released matrix, document the column schema, and cite the file-level identifier at each point of use in Methods instead of the project root URL.

gaps.where: C4, C16, C22 (ggraph), C23, C26 (bowtie2 within the Nextflow workflow), C35 (pipe4C), C36 (IGV)
gaps.missing: Version pins are dense and mostly exact across the paper, but seven steps carry none. The Babraham RNA-seq platform pipeline (C23) is named only as 'their pipeline' with no tool list, version or reference. The calibrated CUT&Tag mapping (C26) is 'a Nextflow implementation of bowtie2' with no workflow name, no Nextflow version and no bowtie2 version. pipe4C (C35) and IGV (C36) are cited without version or commit. ggplot2 is pinned in some sections (v3.5.1, v3.5.2) but not in C16 or C25. There is no R version, no Bioconductor release, and no sessionInfo().
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table listing an exact version (and git commit where the tool is used from a branch, e.g. the HiCUP 'combinations' branch) for every tool, plus R version, Bioconductor release and full sessionInfo() for the R stack; name and version the Babraham platform pipeline and the Nextflow workflow.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, conda/mamba environment file, renv.lock, Nextflow config or requirements file is claimed anywhere. The stack spans command-line C tools (bowtie2, samtools, MACS2, bwtool, fastp, TrimGalore), Python (deepTools), Perl (HiCUP), R/Bioconductor (CHiCAGO, DESeq2, clusterProfiler, GOSemSim, dtwclust, SpiecEasi, ppclust, igraph, plotgardener, data.table, ggplot2, rstatix, org.Hs.eg.db, AnnotationDbi) and a Nextflow workflow - with no dependency closure captured for any of them. This is why capture_claim is exact_pins_partial rather than env_lock_claimed despite the unusually thorough per-package pinning.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a container digest (or a conda-lock / renv.lock pair) covering the command-line, Python, Perl and R stacks, and reference it from the availability statement; ship the Nextflow pipeline with its nextflow.config and a pinned container per process.

gaps.where: Stochastic and human-in-the-loop steps C15 (SparCC), C18 (dtwclust k selection), C19 (K-means k = 5), C22 (igraph layouts and 50-subgraph subsampling), C30 (replicate merging)
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported anywhere in the paper. SparCC bootstrapping, dtwclust partitioning, K-means initialisation, the Kamada-Kawai and Fruchterman-Reingold layouts and the 'subsampled 50 random disjoint subgraphs' are all stochastic. Worse, two decisions are explicitly human-in-the-loop and unrecorded: the choice of k = 6 in C18 was made 'based on inspection of cluster trajectories' with clusters 2 and 6 then merged post hoc, and in C30 'two replicates each for PROTAC and UNC1999 were merged to balance the sequencing depths' without stating which replicates. Neither the cluster labels nor the differential-connectivity result is reproducible from prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Report seeds for every stochastic call, publish the clustering driver scripts including the k-selection and post-hoc merge, and state exactly which replicates were merged in the PRC2 differential analysis.

gaps.where: Reference genomes and annotations (C1, C9, C24, C26, C36)
gaps.missing: 'GRCh38' is used throughout without a patch level, analysis-set flavour or source URL, and no bowtie2 index build recipe or checksum is given; the spike-in genome is given as 'BDGP6' with no Ensembl release. Annotation pins are inconsistent: TSS annotation in C9 uses GENCODE v36 while gene quantification in C24 uses Gencode v47, with no explanation of the mismatch. The ENCODE cCRE decoration matrix (C16) is a bare download URL with no release or access date, and the UCSC encodeCcreCombined track carries no download date. VISTA (C17) has no snapshot date. The GO database behind clusterProfiler/GOSemSim (C21) has no release. The 4DN Hi-C dataset in C36 is properly pinned (4DNFI2YA1USU).
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the exact GRCh38 analysis set and BDGP6 Ensembl release with URLs and checksums, publish the aligner index provenance, justify or harmonise the GENCODE v36 / v47 split, and record a download date plus checksum for the ENCODE cCRE matrix, the UCSC track, the VISTA export and the GO/OrgDb releases.

gaps.where: Externally hosted, moving resources: OSF project https://osf.io/evcy6/, HiCUP 'combinations' branch, pipe4C repository, ENCODE downloads.wenglab.org, UCSC track, VISTA Enhancer Browser, 4DN portal
gaps.missing: Six of the seven external resources track a moving target. The OSF link is a live project root, not a registration, so its contents can change or be withdrawn. The HiCUP dependency is pinned to a *branch* ('tree/combinations') plus a version string rather than a commit hash, so the code actually run cannot be recovered if the branch advances or is deleted. pipe4C is a bare repository URL with no commit. The ENCODE cCRE matrix filename embeds a version ('.matrix.1.gz') but no dated release. VISTA and the UCSC track are continuously curated web resources cited without snapshot dates.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace the OSF project link with a frozen OSF registration DOI; cite HiCUP and pipe4C by commit hash (and archive both to Software Heritage); deposit the exact downloaded ENCODE/UCSC/VISTA files with checksums and access dates as supplementary data.

gaps.missing: The scale-factor definition is missing from the machine-readable text entirely. The Methods sentence reads verbatim 'Scale factors were calculated as follows : .' with the formula rendered as an inline image object. Since every calibrated H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub bigWig (C27), every downstream pileup (C28) and the density profiles (C29) depend on this normalisation, the central quantitative claim of the PRC2-perturbation section cannot be recomputed from the text.
gaps.how_to_close: Write the scale-factor formula out in text (or as MathML) rather than as an image, state whether human or spike-in read counts form the denominator, and release the per-sample spike-in and human read counts alongside the computed factors.
